evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that the quantitative evaluation found limited impacts on household food security, resilience coping, and dietary diversity, and that implementation problems needed correction before scaling up.
evidence.title: The impact of the cash transfer intervention in the commune of Nsele in Kinshasa
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that the quantitative evaluation found limited impacts on household food security, resilience coping, and dietary diversity, and that implementation problems needed correction before scaling up.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Impact evaluation with explicit negative findings and implementation diagnosis.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is about a government-supported social protection effort, but the weakness is mainly implementation-level.
contrary_evidence: The qualitative interviews were more positive and the report notes lessons for future targeting.

evidence.claim: WFP said food and nutrition security in the DRC is hit by conflict, epidemics, climate events, weak infrastructure, and underinvestment in agriculture, health, and human capital.
evidence.title: Democratic Republic of the Congo Country Strategic Plan (2021–2026)
evidence.excerpt: WFP said food and nutrition security in the DRC is hit by conflict, epidemics, climate events, weak infrastructure, and underinvestment in agriculture, health, and human capital.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary WFP country strategy with a plain-language diagnosis of constraints.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a structural baseline, not purely ruler-caused, but it frames the incumbent's constraints.
contrary_evidence: The same plan says WFP supports government priorities rather than substituting for them.

evidence.claim: The World Bank said the DRC had significant gender gaps in school attendance and learning outcomes, and that the resulting analysis helped design the Girls' Learning and Empowerment Project.
evidence.title: Empowering Girls and Enhancing Learning in the Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said the DRC had significant gender gaps in school attendance and learning outcomes, and that the resulting analysis helped design the Girls' Learning and Empowerment Project.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: World Bank results page with explicit link from evidence to policy design.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the Ministry of Finance and education authorities are involved, but this is still donor-led analysis.
contrary_evidence: The page shows the baseline problem was severe in 2017 and needed targeted intervention.

evidence.claim: UNESCO reported that basic education access expanded since 2016, but net enrolment was still only 69 percent, quality was weak because of underfunding and poor infrastructure, and 73 percent of Grade 6 students fell below minimum reading benchmarks.
evidence.title: Spotlight on basic education completion and foundational learning: Democratic Republic of Congo
evidence.excerpt: UNESCO reported that basic education access expanded since 2016, but net enrolment was still only 69 percent, quality was weak because of underfunding and poor infrastructure, and 73 percent of Grade 6 students fell below minimum reading benchmarks.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNESCO knowledge-platform report summarizing a national education diagnosis with specific indicators.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: this is a national education baseline rather than a pure ruler effect, but it frames feasible improvement.
contrary_evidence: The same report says access had expanded, so the picture is mixed rather than uniformly negative.

evidence.claim: UNDP said the project sought to make state entities more accountable to the whole population, including LGBTI people, and to support better laws, more responsive public services, and rights-affirming social norms.
evidence.title: Inclusive Governance Initiative Democratic Republic of the Congo Baseline Report
evidence.excerpt: UNDP said the project sought to make state entities more accountable to the whole population, including LGBTI people, and to support better laws, more responsive public services, and rights-affirming social norms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNDP baseline report with clear human-rights and service-delivery objectives.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the report is about state accountability and inclusion, but it is a project baseline rather than an outcome evaluation.
contrary_evidence: The same report is only a baseline assessment, so it does not prove delivery.

evidence.claim: WHO said the North Kivu Ebola outbreak ended after no additional cases were found, and that 550 people in the affected health zone had been vaccinated using ring strategy, with frontline health workers forming most of the vaccinated group.
evidence.title: Ebola Virus Disease - Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: WHO said the North Kivu Ebola outbreak ended after no additional cases were found, and that 550 people in the affected health zone had been vaccinated using ring strategy, with frontline health workers forming most of the vaccinated group.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct WHO outbreak bulletin with response metrics and a dated end-of-outbreak determination.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tied to crisis response in eastern DRC.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the response was led by the national health ministry with WHO and partners under the incumbent administration.
contrary_evidence: The bulletin credits the Ministry of Health and partners, so ruler-level attribution is indirect.

evidence.claim: In Kasai-Central, UNICEF and villagers rebuilt Lunyenga Primary School in three months; the school was one of 22 built with community help, after more than 550 schools had been destroyed and over 100,000 students were left without classrooms.
evidence.title: Building schools together with communities
evidence.excerpt: In Kasai-Central, UNICEF and villagers rebuilt Lunyenga Primary School in three months; the school was one of 22 built with community help, after more than 550 schools had been destroyed and over 100,000 students were left without classrooms.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 UNICEF account with specific reconstruction counts, timing, and student impact.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and relevant to education recovery from violence and displacement.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the rebuilding was done by UNICEF and communities, but it shows the administration's education-recovery environment and ability to enable local delivery.
contrary_evidence: The destruction was driven by prior conflict; the article does not isolate central-government funding as the sole driver of recovery.

evidence.claim: UNICEF said the DRC had about five million internally displaced persons, including 700,000 displaced in 2022 alone, and that 3.2 million children aged 6 to 11 were out of school; the joint programme in Tanganyika was presented as a model for girls' access and post-conflict recovery.
evidence.title: Education Cannot Wait and UNICEF with partners call for substantial increase in funding for crisis-affected children in the Democratic Republic of the Congo
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF said the DRC had about five million internally displaced persons, including 700,000 displaced in 2022 alone, and that 3.2 million children aged 6 to 11 were out of school; the joint programme in Tanganyika was presented as a model for girls' access and post-conflict recovery.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct 2022 UNICEF press release with clear casualty/displacement and schooling figures plus a government-linked programme example.
evidence.period_fit: Directly in 2022 and tightly relevant to crisis-linked education deprivation and response.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Moderate: the figures largely reflect conflict and displacement pressures, but the programme operates in the national education environment under Tshisekedi.
contrary_evidence: The main causes are conflict and displacement, so this is partly a context source rather than a pure ruler-performance measure.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 nuclear/existential-risk decision by Tshisekedi is evidenced, and the package never shows operational nuclear control, brinkmanship, or safeguard intervention.
Direct 2022 execution and household/distribution outcome evidence remains thinner than the policy and macro coverage.
Direct, nationally representative 2022 welfare-outcome evidence attributable to Tshisekedi remains limited relative to the amount of partner-led program evidence.

Direct personal-nexus evidence is still sparse: no clear 2022 asset-declaration, campaign-finance, beneficial-ownership, or court/audit record ties Tshisekedi himself to self-dealing or deliberate deception.
Independent, audited delivery and outcome evidence is thinner than the program rhetoric and internal reporting.
